name: Fast Distributed Inference Serving for Large Language Models
problem: Run-to-completion processing of LLM requests causes head-of-line blocking: one long request stalls everything behind it, so latency is high even when aggregate throughput is fine.
mechanism: FastServe exploits the autoregressive pattern to make preemption possible at the granularity of each output token, rather than only at request boundaries. Scheduling uses a skip-join multi-level feedback queue: in the paper's 'semi-information-agnostic' setting, only input length is known at arrival, so each arriving job is assigned an initial queue and higher-priority queues are SKIPPED rather than joined, cutting demotions. Adds GPU memory management that proactively offloads and uploads intermediate state to host memory.
speedup_reported: Per the arXiv abstract, versus vLLM: up to 31.4x higher throughput and 17.9x higher throughput under the same average and tail latency requirements respectively. CRITICAL CAVEAT: the 31.4x figure is measured against vLLM under run-to-completion-style configurations and is a single-workload best case, not a general speedup — vLLM's own PagedAttention landed in the same period. Treat this number as 'the gap between two 2023 pre-PagedAttention-defaults engines under latency constraints', not as a durable 3-10x advantage over modern vLLM.
notes:
Venue NOT verified — arXiv only, no venue in the comment field, and I did not find a proceedings page. Recorded as arxiv-preprint deliberately. Do not confuse with 'FastServe: Fast Multi-Model Inference with Anthropic', a different paper. Notably, this is the same group (Yinmin Zhong, Peking University) that later wrote DistServe; the two papers form a decade-scale thread from run-to-completion to phase disaggregation.
